claims.claim: P and S waves are body waves traveling through Earth; P waves are compressional and faster, while S waves are shear and arrive later.
S waves do not travel through liquid, whereas P waves can travel through solid and liquid material.
Surface waves travel along Earth’s surface, arrive later than body waves, and are generally among the largest recorded waves.
The time difference between P and S arrivals at a station can be used to estimate distance to an earthquake; several stations are needed to locate it on a map.
A seismogram records ground motion and can show wave arrivals, but interpretation requires distinguishing earthquake signals from other vibration or recording noise.
